newsitem.title: FRANCE: Carrefour sees '97 meat sales recovering.
newsitem.headline: Carrefour sees '97 meat sales recovering.

text.p: French retailer Carrefour said on Monday meat sales, excluding poultry, should bounce back in 1997 to levels seen in 1995 but that the mad cow crisis hit sales by at least 500 million francs in 1996.
"It lost us at least 500 million francs in sales in 1996 compared with 1995," Luc de Noirmont, Carrefour's managing director for food, told Reuters at a news conference in Paris.
Sales of meat at Carrefour totalled more than three billion francs in 1995.

He also said Carrefour would launch a widespread information campaign from March to try and boost consumption of beef, which fell 11 percent in 1996, chiefly on concerns about bovine spongiform encephalopathy, or mad cow disease.
